html:
The sacred book of the K'iche' Maya of highland Guatemala, telling how the world and people were made and how the K'iche' kings came to rule. It was written down in the K'iche' language but in Latin letters in the 1550s, by K'iche' nobles who wanted to keep an older book alive after the Spanish conquest.

Its main parts:

  • The gods make the world, then try to make people from mud and from wood, and fail.
  • The Hero Twins, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, beat the lords of the underworld, Xibalba, at the ballgame and by trickery, and rise as the sun and moon.
  • The gods finally make humans from maize dough.
  • The K'iche' lineages migrate and found their kingdom.

The original is lost. The only copy is one made around 1701 by the Dominican friar Francisco Ximénez in Chichicastenango, with a Spanish translation, now in Chicago's Newberry Library. With the Dresden Codex and the texts in Maya script, it is a key window on Maya belief.
